metadata.note: Real progress recap of C:\Users\kavya\OneDrive\Desktop\CabStream, grounded in that repo's actual git log. This reel covers WEEK 3 ONLY (commits 2026-06-23 through 2026-06-29, confirmed via `git log --all --format='%ad %h %s' --date=short`): four commits, all on 06-29 (06-23 through 06-28 are silent). 4e93378 (18:55): Databricks cluster (auto-terminate) + Key Vault secret scope. 89566e0 (19:19): fix -- removed dynamic data sources causing a provider bootstrapping error. a99d715 (20:16): fix -- added prevent_destroy to storage account/containers (storage.tf's own new comment explains why: Bronze/Silver/Gold Delta tables are written once, read forever; storage must survive `terraform destroy` between sessions even though compute gets destroyed each session). df47dac (22:44): the big one -- databricks/01_bronze_ingestion.py (493 lines) and 02_silver_processing.py (104 lines), described in the commit message itself as 'Bronze ingestion (1.57B rows) and Silver yellow taxi processing (252.3M rows)'. This is the actual Phase 2 scale verification that weeks 1 and 2 explicitly flagged as NOT YET HAPPENED. Honest scope caveat, directly supported by file-level evidence: the 1.57B/252.3M figures are AS DESCRIBED IN KAVYA'S OWN COMMIT MESSAGE, not independently re-run or re-verified by this reel -- this reel did not execute the Databricks notebook itself. The script's own first cell tests a single known-good month (Jan 2023, verified against a local count of 3,066,766 rows) before scaling to the full 2019-2026 range -- that specific anchor number IS visible directly in the committed script text. Built to satisfy docs/FELLOWS-SUBMISSION.md's required-content rules: the required intro line opens B00's narration verbatim, AI-narration is disclosed in the same beat, and this reel renders native 16:9 (3840x2160) and 9:16 (2160x3840) -- compiled with explicit --height 2160 / --height 3840 from the start, after a resolution bug (compile.py's 720p default) was found and fixed across the rest of this series on 2026-10-29.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my third week building CabStream, a real-time data pipeline project. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Week one was a local pipeline. Week two defined the cloud infrastructure in code, but never ran it. Week three: the pipeline actually ran. Did it hold up at real scale, or did something break the first time it mattered?

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: week three wasn't another quiet infra week like the last one. The pipeline actually ran — described in my own commit message as one-point-five-seven billion rows ingested. That's the number weeks one and two both said wasn't here yet.

beats.narration_text: Four things, all the same night. A Databricks cluster went up, set to auto-terminate, with a Key Vault secret scope attached. Two real bugs surfaced and got fixed — a provider bootstrapping error, then a data-loss gap in the storage config. Bronze ingestion ran: NYC taxi data, 2019 through 2026. And Silver processing ran right after it.

beats.narration_text: What week three didn't have: my own re-verification. One-point-five-seven billion rows is what my commit message says, not a number I re-ran and watched land myself. What I can confirm directly: the ingestion script tests one known month first, January twenty twenty-three, against a locally verified count, before it ever scales up. That discipline is visible in the code. The total isn't independently checked here.

beats.narration_text: Recap: a Databricks cluster went up, two real infra bugs got fixed the same night, and Bronze plus Silver ingestion ran — described in my own commit as one-point-five-seven billion rows and two-hundred-fifty-two-point-three million rows. The honest caveat: that total is what the commit message says, not something this reel re-ran and verified. What's directly confirmed in the code: a known-good test month, checked before anything scaled up. Week three is where the scale arrived — carefully, not blindly.
